Also confirmed 009.jpg total as 26.60.

Turn 22 printed OCR text for 009.jpg, confirming “TakeOut Total (incl GST) 26.60” / “Total Rounded 26.60”.

Turn 23 launched another refinement of total extraction (explicitly detecting/ skipping GST/TAX summary blocks, adjusting priorities). Output again streamed due to soft timeouts (Turns 24–27). This refined run fixed the earlier regressions: 011.jpg returned 15.00; 071.jpg returned 17.70; 077.jpg returned 23.25; 078.jpg returned 92.80; 097.jpg remained 21.00. The full refined list printed across Turns 23–27 included:
007 2019-01-23 20.00; 009 2018-01-18 26.60; 010 2017-12-29 14.10; 011 2017-06-15 15.00; 019 2018-03-18 86.00; 034 2018-08-09 332.30; 039 2018-03-30 189.75; 052 2018-03-23 10.00; 063 2018-02-26 85.54; 064 2018-02-21 1.00; 069 2018-02-20 9.90; 071 2018-02-19 17.70; 074 2018-03-20 102.00; 077 2017-10-29 23.25; 078 2017-02-02 92.80; 080 2017-09-21 10.40; 083 2017-05-30 18.80; 087 2017-07-27 538.00; 088 2017-08-09 99.80; 090 2017-03-13 5.00; 094 2018-02-09 5.90; 097 2016-01-12 21.00.

Turn 28 started a script to generate /app/workspace/stat_ocr.xlsx using openpyxl with one sheet titled “results” and columns [filename, date, total_amount], computing OCR+date+total for each file in sorted filename order. Turns 28–30 show the Excel generation script still running under repeated “soft timeout” observations; no completion message or file verification yet in this window.
</summary>
